title: Exploring Dendritic Computation in Bio-Inspired Architectures for Dynamic Programming
problem: Finding shortest paths in graphs using bio-inspired neuromorphic architectures rather than conventional sequential algorithms. Neuromorphic systems offer alternative computational paradigm with different efficiency/latency tradeoffs.
motivation: Bio-inspired computing leverages dendritic mechanisms (delay lines, feedback) as computational primitives enabling novel algorithm implementations.
method: Model each graph node as leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neuron with dendritic delay line for synaptic propagation and somatic feedback controlling delay. Formulate shortest path as finding earliest neuron firing times, decomposing into sub-problems iteratively solved via backward tracing. Countdown counters implement forward propagation; eligibility traces incorporate edge costs.
key_novelty: Formulating dynamic programming shortest path in spiking neural networks using spike timing as solution mechanism.
contributions: Novel mapping of dynamic programming to dendritic spiking neural systems
Demonstrated scalability on real-world graph instances
FPGA prototyping on Virtex UltraScale validating approach
limitations: Comparative performance metrics (latency, energy, accuracy) versus traditional approaches not discussed in abstract.
